title: SuffixArray hides its integer width behind a struct
body:
`SuffixArray` in `libsufr/src/lib.rs` is `pub enum SuffixArray { U32(Index<u32>), U64(Index<u64>) }`, and `Index<T>` is public with public fields, so the integer width is on the public surface and the docs tell a reader to use `Index` to pick it. The CLI never matches a variant.

## Proposal

```rust
pub struct SuffixArray { inner: SuffixArrayKind }
pub(crate) enum SuffixArrayKind { U32(TypedSuffixArray<u32>), U64(TypedSuffixArray<u64>) }
pub(crate) struct TypedSuffixArray<T: Int> { … }   // today's Index<T>
```

The public methods stay as they are. The three matches in `Hits` move onto `SuffixArray` as `pub(crate)` methods, so every forwarding match is in `lib.rs`. `Index`, `Int` and `FileAccess` leave the crate root. `libsufr/tests/header.rs` opens through `SuffixArray`.

## Rejected

- dev's `Box<dyn SuffixArrayTrait>`: two impls, no generic consumer, a vtable call per search.
- A width parameter on the public type: the user would pick the width, which is what the wrapper exists to prevent.
close_reason: Landed as c6c9b53 on refactor: SuffixArray is a struct over the pub(crate) enum SuffixArrayKind, Index<T> is TypedSuffixArray<T> in typed.rs, and Index, Int and FileAccess left the crate root. Sweep of 7,376 runs identical in stdout, exit codes and .sufr bytes.
